Alright, I need to make sure the agent correctly recognizes when the test suite reports success. Earlier I inserted a regular expression into src/core/agent.ts that looks for phrases like “tests now pass” or “all tests pass”. The current pattern is:

```
|tests? (?:now )?pass|all tests pass)/i;
```

From the latest run output I see a line:

```
✦ The tests now all pass.
```

My existing regex will match “tests now pass” but it won’t match “tests now all pass” because the word “all” isn’t accounted for. That means the agent might miss this success signal, potentially causing it to keep looking for failures that have already been resolved.

I need to broaden the pattern to accept an optional “all” after the optional “now”. Also, the spaces should be flexible – using `\s+` instead of a literal space will handle any amount of whitespace. So the revised pattern should allow:

- “tests pass”
- “tests now pass”
- “tests all pass”
- “tests now all pass”

A concise way to express that is:

```
|tests?\s+(?:now\s+)?(?:all\s+)?pass|all tests pass)/i;
```

Here:
- `tests?\s+` matches “test ” or “tests ” followed by at least one whitespace.
- `(?:now\s+)?` makes “now ” optional.
- `(?:all\s+)?` makes “all ” optional.
- Then `pass` completes the phrase.
- The alternative `all tests pass` remains unchanged.

I’ll apply this change directly in agent.ts, replacing the old string with the new one. Since I only want to modify that specific occurrence, I’ll set `replace_all` to false and target the exact `old_string`. This should tighten the success detection without affecting any other logic.

Proceeding with the edit now.
